title: First Shipment
story:
NORA: `OUTBOUND QUEUE: 0 IMAGES. DEPOT: ONLINE. kestrel/beacon:1.0: LOCAL ONLY.`

The depot is up on port 5000, but the beacon image Amara built exists only on this one machine's disk. If the disk goes, the image goes with it, and Ingrid wants every instrument host to fetch its images from the depot instead.

Publish `kestrel/beacon:1.0` to the depot, under the registry's own address, so anyone on the station can pull it.
objectives: The depot's catalog lists the repository `kestrel/beacon` with the tag `1.0`
startingState: The `depot` registry is running on port 5000 and the image `kestrel/beacon:1.0` is built locally. The depot is empty.
hints: Docker decides where to push by reading the registry host out of the image name. An image called `kestrel/beacon` means Docker Hub; to reach the depot, the same image needs a second name that starts with the registry's address.
Add the name with `docker tag SOURCE TARGET`, where TARGET is `HOST:PORT/repo/name:tag`. Then `docker push TARGET`. You can read back what the depot holds at `http://localhost:5000/v2/_catalog`.

```bash
docker tag kestrel/beacon:1.0 localhost:5000/kestrel/beacon:1.0
docker push localhost:5000/kestrel/beacon:1.0

curl http://localhost:5000/v2/kestrel/beacon/tags/list
```

files.content:
FROM nginx:alpine
LABEL station=kestrel role=beacon
COPY index.html /usr/share/nginx/html/index.html

validation.description: The depot has the tag `1.0` for `kestrel/beacon`
The manifest for `kestrel/beacon:1.0` can be fetched from the depot

debrief: The registry host is part of an image's name, so pushing somewhere new always starts with `docker tag`. Pro tip: a tag is only a pointer, so tagging costs nothing and the push uploads each layer once.
